title: Reading from a file with ifstream

visuals.title: Reading a file: the read position moves forward after every >> (made-up file layout)

steps.note: The file is opened for reading. It holds the text 5 10 15. The read position starts at the first number.
Two variables are created. sum starts at 0.
in >> x reads the number at the cursor into x and moves the cursor forward. The read worked, so the condition is true.
sum becomes 5.
The next number, 10, is read. The cursor moves again.
sum becomes 15.
The last number, 15, is read. The cursor now sits at the end of the file.
sum becomes 30.
There is nothing left to read, so in >> x FAILS and the condition is false. The loop stops. This is why while (in >> x) is the correct loop and while (!in.eof()) can read one value too many.

visuals.title: The correct reading loop: the read IS the condition

stages.name: 1. Open and check
stages.detail: ifstream in("data.txt"); if (!in) { ... }  The file must exist, in the working folder.

stages.name: 2. Try to read
stages.detail: while (in >> x): the program tries to read one value. If it works the condition is true.

stages.name: 3. Use the value
stages.detail: Inside the loop x holds a real value: add it, print it, count it.

stages.name: 4. End of file
stages.detail: When there is nothing left to read, in >> x fails, the condition becomes false and the loop stops. No extra round.

visuals.title: Match each reading tool to its job

pairs.meaning: Reads one value, skipping spaces and new lines
Reads a whole line, spaces included
Loop that stops by itself at the end of the file
Risky loop: often handles the last item twice
Reads one record with three fields
The file could not be opened (missing or wrong folder)

goal: After this you can read numbers, words, lines and whole records from a text file with the correct loop, and avoid the classic end-of-file bug.
warmup: A teacher reads out the marks sheet one name after another until the sheet ends. She does not ask "is the sheet finished?" before every name. She just keeps reading, and when there is nothing to read she stops. The right file loop works the same way: try to read, and if the reading worked, use the value.
definition: To read a file you create an ifstream: ifstream in("data.txt");. The file must already exist. The operator >> works like cin >>: it skips spaces and new lines and reads one value (an int, a double, a word). getline(in, line) reads a whole line, including spaces, into a string. Both can be used as the condition of a while loop, because a read that fails (end of file, or wrong kind of data) makes the stream false. So while (in >> x) means "keep going while a value was successfully read" and while (getline(in, line)) means "keep going while a line was successfully read".
howItWorks: Follow the first trace. The loop condition itself performs the read. When the file is finished, the read fails, the condition is false and the loop stops. Nothing is processed twice. Compare with the bug: while (!in.eof()). The flag eof only turns true AFTER a read has already failed, so the body runs one extra time with an old or useless value. That is why the notes say: put the read in the condition. For records, read all fields in one condition: while (in >> roll >> name >> marks). This works when every record has the same fields in the same order, separated by spaces. Use >> when values are separated by spaces. Use getline when you need the whole line, for example to count lines or to read text that contains spaces. To count words, read with >> into a string: each >> takes one word. In all samples the program first creates its own input file, so it runs the same everywhere.

sample.title: Read numbers and add them

explanation.text: Setup: we create the input file ourselves so the program is complete.
Four numbers on one line, separated by spaces.
Opens the file for reading.
Always check that the file opened.
x receives each number from the file.
sum collects the total. It must start at 0.
Reads one number. If the read works, the loop runs. At the end of the file the read fails and the loop stops.
Adds the number just read.
Prints the total after the loop.

steps.note: nums.txt is created for writing.
The four numbers are written on one line, separated by spaces.
Now the file is opened for reading. The reading position is at the very start.
sum starts at 0, like a empty bucket.
in >> x tries to read a number. It works, so the condition is true. x = 10.
Shows the number just read.
Next number: x = 20. (sum += x makes sum 30.)
Shows 20.
Next number: x = 30. (sum becomes 60.)
Shows 30.
Next number: x = 40. (sum becomes 100.)
Shows 40.
The next in >> x finds no more numbers, so it FAILS and the condition is false. The loop stops, with no extra pass.
The total of all numbers in the file.

sample.expectedOutput:
Line 1: Ali scored well
Line 2: Sana did better
Line 3: Usman tried

explanation.text: Setup: three lines of text with 3, 3 and 2 words.
getline reads a full line, spaces included, until there are no more lines.
Each successful getline is one line.
To read the same file a second time we open it again, so reading starts from the beginning.
>> into a string reads one word (it stops at a space or a new line).
Each successful read is one word.

worked.problem: Exam question: students.txt holds records in the form roll name marks. Read all records, print them, then print how many students there are, the average marks and the name of the topper.
pseudocode: WHILE a record (roll, name, marks) can be read: PRINT it, add marks to total, count = count + 1, IF marks > best THEN remember best and name
IF count > 0: PRINT count, total / count and the topper

sample.title: Reading records with several fields
sample.expectedOutput:
101 - Ali - 78
102 - Sana - 91
103 - Usman - 66
104 - Hira - 88
Students: 4
Average: 80.75
Top: Sana with 91

explanation.text: Setup: one record per line, fields separated by spaces.
One variable for each field of the record.
total adds up all the marks.
best remembers the highest mark seen so far.
Reads one whole record. If any of the three reads fails (end of file) the loop stops.
Shows the record that was just read.
A new highest mark: remember it and the name.
Avoids dividing by zero when the file is empty.
total / count: total is a double, so the division keeps decimals.

variations.when: Numbers or single words separated by spaces.
Whole lines (they may contain spaces), counting lines.
Read the file a second time from the start.
AVOID. Often processes the last item twice.

mistakes.error: No compiler error. The file holds 5 10 15 but the program prints: 5 10 15 15 . The last number appears twice, because eof() becomes true only after a read has failed. Put the read inside the loop condition.

mistakes.right:
ifstream in("data.txt");
if (!in) { cout << "File not found!" << endl; return 1; }
mistakes.error: No compiler error. If the file is missing the loop silently runs zero times and the program prints nothing useful. Check the file first.

mistakes.wrong:
// file lines look like: Sana 91
while (in >> roll >> marks) n++;
mistakes.right: while (in >> name >> marks) n++;   // same order as in the file
mistakes.error: No compiler error. Reading in the wrong order fails at once (the word Sana is not a number), so the loop never runs. In our check it counted 0 records. The variables must match the order and type of the fields in the file.
The compiler reports error: no match for 'operator<<' (operand types are 'std::ifstream' {aka 'std::basic_ifstream<char>'} and 'int'). An ifstream reads, so use >> with it. << is for output streams.

mistakes.right:
int x;
while (in >> x) total += x;
mistakes.error: The compiler says x was not declared in this scope. Declare the variable that receives the data before the loop.

examTips: Write while (in >> x) or while (getline(in, line)). Never while (!in.eof()). The notes mark the eof loop as a bug.
For records read all fields in one condition: while (in >> roll >> name >> marks).
Start total at 0 and count at 0 before the loop. Check count > 0 before dividing.
Use getline to count lines, >> to count words, and remember that getline keeps the spaces.
To read the same file again, close it and open it again (or open a second stream).
romanSummary: ifstream in("data.txt"); file parhne ke liye kholta hai. File pehle se maujood honi chahiye, isliye if (!in) se check karein.
in >> x space ya nayi line tak ek value parhta hai, getline(in, line) poori line parhta hai.
Sahi loop: while (in >> x) ya while (getline(in, line)). Parhna hi condition mein likhein, file khatam hote hi loop khud ruk jata hai.
while (!in.eof()) se bachein, aksar aakhri value do baar process ho jati hai.
Record ke liye while (in >> roll >> name >> marks) likhein, fields ki tarteeb file jaisi ho.

practice.hint: The eof flag turns true only after a failed read.
practice.explanation: After reading 3 the flag is still false, so the loop runs once more: the count is 4, not 3.

practice.hint: Move the read into the condition.
practice.explanation: eof() is true only after a failed read. Reading in the condition avoids the extra round.

practice.hint: The function that reads a whole line.
practice.explanation: getline(in, line) reads one line and is false at the end of the file.
